title: Cylindrical rod
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw the first loop as a circle centered at coordinates [0.0188, 0.0188] with a radius of 0.0188. Draw the second loop as another circle with the same center but a smaller radius of 0.015. Scale the entire sketch by a factor of 0.0375. Rotate the scaled sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The final dimensions of the cylindrical rod with a rectangular cross-section at one end are: length of 0.0375 units, width of 0.0375 units, and height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a circular face
r = r.circle(0.0188)

# Create a circular face with a smaller radius
r = r.circle(0.015)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical rod
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Scale the sketch (this step is not necessary as the scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion)
# r = r.scale(0.0375)

# Translate the object to the specified position
r = r.translate((0.0188, 0.0188, 0.0))

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0188, 0.0188)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0188)         # Draw the outer circle
    .circle(0.015)          # Draw the inner circle
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

height = 0.7500

    cq.Workplane("XY")
